elements.text: Flank pain with leucocytes/nitrites on dipstick and any of: vomiting, BP < 90/60, pulse ≥ 100, diabetes, male, pregnant or post menopause: complicated pyelonephritis likely

elements.text: Blood/protein in urine with new swelling of face/feet, BP ≥ 140/90 or passing little urine: kidney disease likely

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with urinary symptoms and any of:
elements.text: Blood in urine and sudden, severe, one-sided pain in flank or groin: kidney stone likely
Manage and refer urgently:
If unable to pass urine, insert urinary catheter.

If kidney disease likely: if pulse > 100 or respiratory rate ≥ 30, give face mask oxygen and furosemide 80mg oral/slow IV, avoid IV fluids. If BP > 150/100, give amlodipine 5mg and furosemide 40mg orally.

If kidney stone likely: give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L IV 6 hourly. If pain severe, give morphine 5-10mg IM or diluted morphine 3-5mg IV. If giving IV, dilute 10mg morphine with 9mL of sodium chloride 0.9%. If needed, give another 1mL/min until pain improved, up to 10mL. Repeat morphine after 4 hours if needed. Stop if BP < 90/60. Discuss/refer.

If complicated pyelonephritis likely: first collect urine for MCS, then give ceftriaxone 1g IV1/IM. Give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L 6 hourly. If BP < 90/60, give additional sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 90. Stop if breathing worsens. Include dose, route and time of ceftriaxone administration in referral letter.
URINARY SYMPTOMS
• If complicated/recurrent UTI or no better, send urine MCS. Review after 2 days: if resistant/no better, discuss/refer. • If blood in urine, treat. Then send urine MCS: if blood persists, refer.

Give ciprofloxacin 500mg 12 hourly for 7 days and paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (max 4g/24 hours). • Advise to return if worse: refer.

Schistosomiasis likely • Notify7. • If fever, cough, headache, or urticaria, refer same day. • If not, give single dose praziquantel 40mg/ kg. • Advise to boil water before use and avoid swimming in contaminated water. • Refer if swelling of face/ feet or blood in urine persists ≥ 2 months after treatment.
